verdict.rationale: Aider has no documented IDE extension or in-editor chat panel. Its own `--watch-files` mode does let you work from your IDE: you write AI comments in files, `AI?` triggers an answer to your question and `AI!` triggers code changes, and a community user confirms this works with a normal editor. This counts as in-IDE interaction, but it is comment-driven rather than a true chat inside the IDE, and the evidence does not show where answers are displayed. Missing for 10: a native IDE plugin or chat panel, in-editor display of responses, and independent corroboration of the contextual-help workflow inside the IDE.

support.subject: As a developer, I can chat with the coding assistant directly inside my IDE for contextual help

citations.quote: If you run aider with `--watch-files`, it will watch all files in your repo and look for any AI coding instructions you add using your favorite IDE or text editor.
AI? triggers aider to answer your question.
Rather than using /add to add a file inside the aider chat, you can simply put an #AI comment in it and save the file.
Aider has a web mode and a 'watch mode', where you can use your normal editor and if you leave a comment like '# make this darker ai!', Aider will step in and apply the change.
